'''Brigitte Luis Guillermo Baptiste'''<ref name="Soho">{{Cite web|url=https://www.soho.co/historias/articulo/hombres-con-tetas-mi-marido-tiene-tetas-y-aun-asi-aprendi-a-ser-feliz/23195/|title=Confesiones de una esposa que aprendió a ser feliz|date=13 May 2011 }}</ref> (born October 23, 1963) is a Colombian cultural [[Landscape ecology|landscape ecologist]] and an expert on environmental issues and [[biodiversity]] in Colombia. She is a member of the Multidisciplinary Expert Panel of the [[Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services|Intergovernmental Science and Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services]] and has been part of the national representation to the [[Inter-American Institute for Global Change Research]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=BBaptiste|url=https://ipbes.net/users/bbaptiste|website=ipbes.net|language=en|access-date=2020-05-02|archive-date=2020-09-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920013431/https://ipbes.net/users/bbaptiste|url-status=dead}}</ref> She served as director of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Biological Resources Research Institute]] from 2011 until 2019.<ref name="Hogan" /> In September 2019, Baptiste became the director of [https://universidadean.edu.co/ Universidad Ean].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Brigitte Baptiste, nueva rectora de la Universidad Ean {{!}} Noticias|url=https://universidadean.edu.co/noticias/brigitte-baptiste-nueva-rectora-de-la-universidad-ean|website=Universidad EAN|language=es|access-date=2020-05-02}}</ref> She considers that queerness and ecology are linked together.<ref name="Smith" />

== Education ==

Baptiste studied biology at the [[Pontifical Xavierian University]], where she graduated with a thesis on the ecology of fishing in [[Araracuara, Colombia|Araracuara]], [[Amazon rainforest|Amazon]].<ref name="lsv" /><ref name="Emblin">{{cite news|last1=Emblin|first1=Richard|title=Baptiste: The heels of Humboldt|url=https://thecitypaperbogota.com/features/baptiste-the-heels-of-humboldt/6458|accessdate=19 November 2017|work=The City Paper Bogotá|date=24 March 2014}}</ref> As a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Scholar]] from 1992 to 1994, she completed a [[master's degree]] in tropical [[Conservation biology|conservation]] and development studies at the [[University of Florida]]. Her thesis concerned forest management by rural communities in Boyacá Andes, Colombia. She continued her graduate studies as part of the Russell Train Program of the [[World Wildlife Fund]] (WWF)<ref name="lsv">{{cite web|title=Brigitte Baptiste|url=http://lasillavacia.com/quienesquien/perfilquien/brigitte-baptiste|website=La Silla Vacía|accessdate=19 November 2017|language=es}}</ref> at the [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]], in Environmental Sciences (Ecological Economics and Natural Resource Management) in 2000. Her dissertation is titled, "The concept of main ecological structure (EEP in spanish) and its potential as environmental management tool for biodiversity".<ref name="cv">{{cite web|title=BRIGITTE LUIS GUILLERMO BAPTISTE|url=http://www.ipbes.net/sites/default/files/CV_MEP2014_Baptiste.pdf|accessdate=19 November 2017}}</ref>

== Professional life ==

Brigitte Baptiste has had a long career in both [[Nonprofit organization|nonprofit]] and academic spheres. As a student in 1982, she co-founded the environmental nonprofit ''Corporación Grupo Ecológico'' GEA, which she would later serve as director from 1984 to 1991. From 1991 to 1996, she served as a professor in the Institute of Environmental Studies and Development (IDEADE) at Pontifical University, during which she edited Ambiente y Desarrollo (IDEADE-PUJ). After 1996, she coordinated the Program for Biodiversity Use and Valuation at the Humboldt Institute and consulted for numerous nonprofits, including [[World Wide Fund for Nature|WWF Colombia]]. She returned to Pontifical University from 2002 to 2009 to teach and research as an assistant professor.<ref name="cv" /> She served as the director of the Humboldt Institute from 2011 to 2019.<ref name="Hogan">{{cite news|last1=Hogan|first1=Mary Margaret|title=Brigitte Baptiste discusses the queering of ecology|url=https://www.umass.edu/hfa/news/brigitte-baptiste-discusses-queering-ecology|accessdate=19 November 2017|work=www.umass.edu|archive-date=8 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308214805/https://www.umass.edu/hfa/news/brigitte-baptiste-discusses-queering-ecology|url-status=dead}}</ref>

As director, Baptiste represented Colombia's scientific authority to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora ([[CITES]]) and Subsidiary Body of Scientific, Technical and Technological Advice ([[Subsidiary Body of Scientific and Technological Advice|SBSTTA]]). She serves on the Intergovernmental Panel on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services ([[Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services|IPBES]]) as a member of its Global Panel of 25 experts (MEP) on behalf of [[Latin America]] and the Caribbean (2015–2017). There, she co-chairs working groups on [[Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Indigenous]] and [[Traditional knowledge|Local Knowledge]], as well as on Policy Tools and Methodologies. She is also a member of the IAI's Science Policy Advisory Committee (Inter-American Environmental Initiative for Global Change) and the scientific committee of the global program PECS (Ecosystem Change and Society).<ref name="lsv" /> She was a prominent voice advocating for a peace deal in the [[Colombian conflict|Colombian Civil War]].<ref name="Smith">{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Jennie Erin |date=8 December 2016 |title=The Queer Ecology of the Colombian Civil War |work=Nautilus |url=http://nautil.us/issue/43/heroes/-the-queer-ecology-of-the-colombian-civil-war |accessdate=19 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180129004600/https://nautil.us/issue/43/heroes/-the-queer-ecology-of-the-colombian-civil-war |archive-date=29 January 2018}}</ref> Baptiste became director of  Universidad Ean in September 2019.<ref name=":0" />

In addition to her academic pursuits, Brigitte Baptiste was featured in an episode of "Taboo" by [[National Geographic]] Latin America.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tabú Latinoamérica 2 Cambio de Género (Parte 1)| website=[[YouTube]] |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lZSpNdgR4R0|accessdate=19 November 2017|date=21 July 2011}}</ref> She is also a [[columnist]] in the economic newspaper ''La República''.<ref name="republica">{{Cite web | url=http://www.larepublica.co/users/brigitte-baptiste |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160806012346/http://www.larepublica.co/users/brigitte-baptiste|archive-date = 2016-08-06|title = Brigitte Baptiste, Análisis sobre economía, finanzas, empresas y negocios de Colombia y el mundo &#124; LaRepublica.co}}</ref>

Her life was portrayed in the book ''Brigitte Baptiste: un homenaje ilustrado'' ({{Lit|Brigitte Baptiste: an illustrated tribute}}).<ref name="HomenajeIlustrado">{{Cite book| publisher = Puntoaparte| isbn = 978-958-52-1072-1| last1 = Baptiste| first1 = Brigitte| last2 = Barragán| first2 = Andrés David| last3 = Torres Carreño| first3 = Guillermo| title = Brigitte Baptiste: un homenaje ilustrado| location = Bogotá| date = 2019}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Baptiste married Adriana Vásquez on December 31, 1999.<ref name="Soho"/> Together they have two daughters, Candelaria and Juana Pasión.<ref name="Dueñas">{{cite news|last1=Dueñas|first1=Jairo|title="Rompí el molde de ser hombre", Brigitte Baptiste|url=https://cromos.elespectador.com/personajes/actualidad/articulo-142233-brigitte-baptiste-rompi-el-molde-de-ser-hombre|accessdate=19 November 2017|date=7 March 2017|language=es|archive-date=5 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905054220/http://cromos.elespectador.com/personajes/actualidad/articulo-142233-brigitte-baptiste-rompi-el-molde-de-ser-hombre|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Emblin" />

==Awards==
In December 2024, Brigitte Baptiste was included on the [[BBC]]'s ''[[100 Women (BBC)|100 Women]]'' list.<ref name=bbc>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/resources/idt-4f79d09b-655a-42f8-82b4-9b2ecebab611|title=BBC 100 Women 2024: Who is on the list this year?|publisher=BBC|date=3 December 2024|accessdate=3 December 2024 |language=}}</ref>
